title: Week of Sep 7 – Sep 13
subtitle: Block 3, Big-4 retest, Week 4: an extra build week, your call. The deload slides to next week. Everything steps up at once: lifts off this week's tops, 25 running miles, and bench gets the first heavy triple on the road to 225.
goals: Why this is a build week and not the deload: you said you weren't fatigued at the end of the sessions and the log agrees. Squat 205×5, RDL 225×8 (ten past the plan), deadlift 275×4 that 'came much easier than expected', OHP 125×5 strict, pull-up max 18 which ties the Block 2 exit. Nothing stalled, nothing hurt. So one more push: Squat 210×5 (215 if the 195 in the ramp moves like a warm-up), RDL 230×8, Deadlift 285×4, OHP 125×5 again but owned instead of strained. Top sets at ~2 RIR, full back protocol on every hinge. The deload is next week (Sep 14–20) and it is not optional after this one: five straight weeks of building since the bridge week is the limit.

Bench, toward 225: this week you held 185 because it 'was feeling too heavy' and unspotted that was the right read. 185×5 puts the estimated single around 215, so 225 is about 5% away, not 2 weeks of casual progress but not far either. The plan from here is bench twice a week and heavier, lower reps: Wed ramps to the first heavy triple, 195×3 at 1–2 RIR, then two back-off fives at 170. Fri adds a second touch, paused bench 3×5 at 160, which builds the bottom position where a 225 single is won or lost. The rough road: deload week keeps bench active with crisp doubles at 185, then 205×2, then a 215 single, then the 225 attempt around the first week of October, fresh, on a Wednesday. If 205×2 flies you can pull it forward a week. One rule with no exceptions: no attempt above 200 without safety arms or pins set at chest height, or a spotter. The full attempt schedule is written into TRAINING_CYCLE.

Running: 25 miles, up from 22.1 this week and 22.7 the week before. Mon 2 + Tue 7 + Wed 2 + Thu 6.5 + Fri 3 + Sun 4.5. Tuesday grows to 5×6 min at threshold; Thursday keeps the steady finish, now 2 miles. About 46 hard minutes on roughly 3.5 aerobic hours, which is the 70/30 lane. The honest flag again: this week's 'easy' Thursday averaged 158 and Sunday 155. At 22 miles that was tolerable. At 25 with four lift days it isn't, so the easy miles are ≤150 this week, and if that means 10:30 pace the morning after intervals, it means 10:30 pace. Tuesday's fourth rep averaged 182 with a max of 190: that is 5K effort, not threshold. Cap the reps at 178.

Lifting volume: 83 planned sets vs 78 planned and 83 logged this week (you added extra pull-up sets and went 3×10 on Friday). Two log notes carried in: pull-ups come off Friday so the Saturday max benchmark isn't the day after a pull-up day (your ask), Friday gets a chest-supported row in that slot instead. And push-ups get more work: 4 sets on Saturday and a bigger dip block, since 30/20/12 left you 'super sore' and wanting more.

Core, floor only, 6+ sets each lift day, rotated off this week: Mon = plank shoulder taps / flutter kicks / side plank, Wed = dead bug / bicycle crunch / plank, Fri (deadlift day, spine-friendly) = bird dog / hollow hold / side plank, Sat = V-up / dead bug / plank.

Food and weight: you're at 190.3 today, and the app's goal line (184.9 by Oct 10) has you about 2.5 lb behind pace after the move and two travel weekends. The deficit dial is currently set at 600, which is not slight, and half the days since Aug 27 have partial logs (546, 890 cal days), so the smart goal is only as honest as the log. Suggested reset, two taps on the weight page: deficit 300 (about 0.5 lb/week, small enough to fuel 25 miles and a bench push), goal 185.0 by Nov 29 from 190.3 today. Log the whole day or don't count the day. Waist Sunday morning, fasted.
review: Retest week, every main lift moved. Squat 205×5 clean. RDL 225×8, ten past the plan. Bench held at 185, your call, and the right one unspotted. OHP 125×5 strict with a strain on the last rep, which is what 0.65×BW at a rep PR should feel like. Deadlift 275×4 with room, on a day you played it safe on purpose. Pull-ups: 3×10/10/9 on Friday when you decided the sixes were too light, then an 18 max on Saturday plus 8 and 6 on follow-on sets, tying the Block 2 exit while running 22 miles. Running: 22.1 miles, Tuesday's 4×6 progressed from 7:16 to 6:54 pace with the last rep at 182 avg HR. That last rep is where the fitness shows and also where the discipline goes; threshold reps should finish feeling repeatable. The week you asked for was 'building on all fronts'. This is what that costs: the easy runs have to actually be easy, and the deload after this one is real.

items.note: Ramp 145/165/180 → top set 195×3 at 1–2 RIR. First heavy triple of the 225 build. 185×5 felt too heavy to step up from, and it should: fives at 185 and triples at 195 are the same effort, the triple is just the honest way to practice heavier bar weight. UNSPOTTED rules: safety arms set, feet planted, never a grind, rack early if the third rep slows badly. If 180 in the ramp feels like a top set, take 190×3 and call it done.
